title: Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Program Acquisition Analyst and Advisor provides acquisition analysis, program management insight, and headquarters integration support to Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. The position requires an experienced Army acquisition professional who understands the Fires portfolio and can apply firsthand program management experience to assess program issues, develop recommendations, and support leadership decisions. The successful candidate will have progressive Army acquisition experience culminating in successful completion of a lieutenant colonel–level Centralized Selection List (CSL) acquisition Product Manager assignment. Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, the Rapid Capabilities and Critical Technologies Office (RCCTO), or PAE Fires is required. This is a hands-on analytical and coordination role. The individual develops decision materials, integrates program and staff inputs, tracks priority actions, and helps translate leadership direction into coordinated follow-through. 
Duties: 
Apply Army acquisition and Fires portfolio experience to analyze program execution, identify issues, and develop practical recommendations for leadership consideration.
Assess program cost, schedule, performance, and risk, identifying dependencies and decisions requiring headquarters attention.
Coordinate priority actions across program offices, portfolio elements, and functional staff; consolidate inputs and track actions through completion.
Prepare and refine briefings, decision papers, read-aheads, talking points, and executive correspondence that clearly explain issues, options, and recommended actions.
Support acquisition reviews, program reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites by coordinating materials, identifying decision requirements, and documenting outcomes.
Analyze the relationships among requirements, acquisition strategies, funding, contracting, testing, fielding, and sustainment to identify execution challenges and inform recommendations.
Support resource prioritization and Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) activities by assessing program needs, funding considerations, and portfolio impacts.
Coordinate with Army requirements organizations, acquisition stakeholders, and mission partners to clarify issues and support alignment across organizational boundaries.
Maintain visibility of leadership decisions, taskings, and commitments; identify delays or unresolved issues and coordinate follow-up.
Recommend improvements to acquisition processes, staff coordination, and portfolio governance based on practical program management experience.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
12 plus year of relevant DoD acquisition experience. 
Progressive experience in Army acquisition and program management, including assignments of increasing responsibility leading to CSL selection and service.
Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, RCCTO, or PAE Fires, with demonstrated knowledge of the Fires portfolio.
Substantive responsibility for acquisition program execution and demonstrated understanding of Fires programs, organizational relationships, capability priorities, and acquisition challenges.
Practical knowledge of the Army acquisition process and the Defense Acquisition System, including acquisition strategy development, milestone decisions, requirements integration, contracting, test and evaluation, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment.
Experience managing program cost, schedule, performance, and risk and presenting program status, issues, and recommendations to acquisition leadership.
Working knowledge of PPBE and the relationship between program execution, funding requirements, and resource decisions.
Demonstrated ability to develop clear briefings, decision papers, and written recommendations for senior leaders.
Ability to coordinate across program offices and functional staffs, reconcile competing inputs, and manage multiple actions with established deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Ability to work onsite in Huntsville, Alabama, and travel approximately 10 percent. 
Must have a current driver's license. 
Must be a U.S. Citizen 
Must have an active U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have a Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this clearance level during their employment 
Education Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in engineering, business, management, public administration, or a related field.
Preferred / Desired Skills : 
Recent experience directly supporting or managing Army Fires acquisition programs.
Experience coordinating with acquisition headquarters and preparing materials for General Officer or Senior Executive Service reviews.
DAWIA Program Management certification at the Advanced level or equivalent prior certification.
Master’s degree in engineering, business, management, public administration, national security, military strategy, acquisition, or a related field.
Experience supporting portfolio reviews, cross-program integration, and resource prioritization.
Active Top Secret clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility.

title: FMS Analyst

title: Senior Acquisition and Contracting Support Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Acquisition and Contracting Support Analyst  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Acquisition and Contracting Support Analyst to serve as a core subject matter expert providing comprehensive, cradle-to-grave contracting advisory and procurement package development support to a PAE Fires, Program Management Office. The successful candidate will translate program technical requirements into compliant, actionable solicitation and contract execution packages in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and agency-specific acquisition instructions. This role supports Procuring Contracting Officers (PCOs), Contracting Officers' Representatives (CORs), and Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) through pre-award strategy formulation, solicitation package assembly, source selection advisory support, and post-award contract administration tracking. 
Duties: 
Performance Work Statements and Specifications: Translate complex government technical needs into legally sufficient, clearly defined Performance Work Statements (PWS), Statements of Work (SOW), and Statements of Objectives (SOO) with measurable Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans (QASPs). 
Data Deliverables (CDRLs): Formulate and tailor Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLs, DD Form 1423) mapped to appropriate Data Item Descriptions (DIDs), ensuring data rights assertions, delivery schedules, and technical reporting mechanisms align with program goals. 
Solicitation Sections L and M: Draft instructions to offerors (Section L) and evaluation criteria and methodologies (Section M) for competitive acquisitions, including Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) and Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selections. 
Statutory and Regulatory Determinations: Draft supporting determination documents for government review and approval, including Determinations and Findings (D&F), Justifications and Approvals (J&A) for other than full and open competition, Sole Source Justifications, and Small Business Subcontracting Plan reviews. 
Cost and Price Modeling Support: Collaborate with government cost estimators to develop Independent Government Cost Estimates (IGCEs), cost breakdown models, and pricing schedules, including Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structuring. 
Market Research: Conduct comprehensive, documented market research across the commercial and defense industrial bases pursuant to FAR Part 10, and draft Market Research Reports (MRRs). 
Industry Outreach and Solicitations: Prepare and coordinate public announcements, including Sources Sought Notices, Requests for Information (RFIs), and Draft Requests for Proposal (RFPs) via SAM.gov and related portals. Synthesize industry feedback to inform government acquisition decisions. 
Acquisition Planning: Draft formal Acquisition Plans (APs) and Acquisition Strategies under FAR Part 7 and DFARS 207. Evaluate contracting mechanisms, including FAR Part 12 (Commercial Products and Commercial Services), FAR Part 15 (Negotiated Procurements), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) task orders, GSA Federal Supply Schedules, and Other Transaction Authority (OTA) consortium models. 
Small Business Utilization: Research and recommend socioeconomic set-aside strategies (8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, and HUBZone) in alignment with agency small business utilization goals. 
Source Selection Advisory Support: Serve as a non-voting technical and procurement advisor to Source Selection Evaluation Boards (SSEBs) and Source Selection Authorities (SSAs), adhering strictly to FAR 15.3 and Procurement Integrity Act (41 U.S.C. 2101-2107) guidelines. 
Compliance Matrix Reviews: Conduct initial compliance reviews of vendor proposals against solicitation requirements, RFP terms, and baseline instructions to identify non-conforming submissions. 
Evaluation Synthesis: Prepare evaluation worksheets, synthesize technical evaluator findings into cohesive strengths, weaknesses, deficiencies, and risk summaries, and draft factual inputs for Government Source Selection Decision Documents (SSDDs). 
Evaluation Notices (ENs): Draft clear, objective ENs and discussion questions for the Contracting Officer to present to competitive range offerors. 
Deliverable Surveillance: Establish and maintain deliverable tracking systems to monitor contractor compliance with CDRLs, contract delivery schedules, and PWS performance metrics. 
Modification Packages: Prepare procurement packages for contract modifications, including supplemental agreements, administrative changes, exercise of option periods, and scope change justifications. 
Performance Monitoring Support: Assist CORs in drafting contractor performance evaluations for submission into the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS). 
Financial and Invoice Tracking: Review vendor invoices and public vouchers via Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) for cost and schedule consistency, labor category alignment, and travel reimbursement compliance. Alert the COR and PCO to cost growth, funding burn-rate anomalies, or period-of-performance risks. 
Contract Closeout: Facilitate administrative contract closeout procedures under FAR 4.804. Inventory deliverables, verify de-obligation amounts, and coordinate final property and patent clearances. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Minimum 8 years of progressive experience providing direct contracting or acquisition support within the Department of Defense (DoD) or Federal Civilian agencies. 
Expert knowledge of the FAR, DFARS, and agency-level supplements. 
Demonstrated proficiency structuring and administering Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee (CPIF), Time-and-Materials (T&M), and IDIQ task and delivery orders. 
Proficiency with standard government procurement platforms, including PIEE/WAWF, Standard Procurement System (SPS)/Procurement Desktop-Defense (PD2)/Contract Writing Systems (CWS), SAM.gov, CPARS, and FPDS-NG. 
Travel: Up to 5 %
Must be a U.S. Citizen
Active Secret clearance is required. Top Secret preferred. 
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Acquisition/Contract Management, Finance, Supply Chain, or a related field. 
Desired Skills : 
Master's degree or MBA. 
NCMA Certified Federal Contract Manager (CFCM) or Certified Professional Contract Manager (CPCM). 
DAWIA Contracting Professional certification (or legacy DAWIA Level II/III in Contracting). 
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

title: HUMS Analyst / Programmer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a HUMS Analyst / Programmer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
PeopleTec is seeking an experienced Health and Usage Monitoring System (HUMS) Analyst / Programmer to provide specialized engineering and software development support for the CheckPoint HUMS Test Station.
The position will support the development, modification, integration, troubleshooting, and validation of HUMS test station software and associated hardware interfaces.
This is a temporary, on-call position requiring specialized knowledge of HUMS ground-based systems, software development, data acquisition, and automated testing.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 
Support development, maintenance, and enhancement of CheckPoint HUMS Test Station software.
Analyze, modify, debug, and test existing software applications.
Develop and integrate software supporting HUMS data acquisition, processing, and analysis.
Support hardware and software interfaces between HUMS equipment and the test station.
Develop automated test procedures, data simulation, and validation capabilities.
Troubleshoot system communication, instrumentation, and data-processing issues.
Support verification and validation of system functionality and software modifications.
Provide technical documentation and recommendations for system improvements.
Collaborate with engineering personnel to support project-specific development and testing requirements.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Demonstrated practical experience with HUMS systems, test station software, and hardware integration is essential.
Previous hands-on experience working with CheckPoint HUMS Test Station systems.
Experience developing, maintaining, or troubleshooting HUMS ground-based systems or associated test equipment.
Software development experience using C++, C#, or similar programming languages.
Experience with hardware/software integration, data acquisition, and automated testing.
Working knowledge of aircraft HUMS systems and associated data-processing requirements.
Ability to independently analyze existing software, troubleshoot issues, and implement technical solutions.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Desired Skills : 
Experience with military rotorcraft HUMS applications and condition-based maintenance systems.
Familiarity with MIL-STD-1553, ARINC-429, IRIG 106, or similar avionics communication and data interfaces.
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing, fault simulation, and automated verification and validation.
Knowledge of vibration analysis, signal processing, and mechanical health monitoring.
Experience with instrumentation, sensor interfaces, and ground support equipment.
Experience with legacy software modification and system modernization.
Employment Conditions : 
This is a temporary, on-call position. Work assignments and hours will be based on project requirements and available funding. No minimum number of work hours is guaranteed.
The employee must be capable of independently performing specialized engineering and software development tasks with minimal supervision.

title: Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a motivated recent Computer Science graduate to join our technical team as an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist (Hybrid / On-Site). In this role, you will help design, build, and maintain data exchange pipelines and application interfaces that connect disparate internal databases and external partner platforms.
You will work closely with cross-functional engineering teams, product managers, and external stakeholders to ensure reliable, automated data flow across systems. This position offers an ideal bridge between core software engineering, data architecture, and technical project coordination.
Essential Job Functions 
Data Integration & Interface Development 
Design, build, and maintain data transformation routines and data exchange schemas (e.g., XML, JSON, REST APIs) to enable seamless communication between heterogeneous software platforms.
Implement parsers, validation routines, and automated import/export pipelines to ensure clean data migration and interoperability across systems.
Modernize legacy data structures and formats by converting them into standardized, scalable web and enterprise schema standards.
Conduct initial testing, debugging, and quality verification on data exchange workflows prior to deployment.
Technical Coordination & Project Support 
Coordinate cross-functional technical syncs and sprint reviews; assist in establishing sprint milestones and tracking team deliverables.
Document meeting notes, track action items, and follow up with internal development teams and external partners on technical requirements and open tickets.
Monitor project deadlines and proactively communicate roadblocks or timeline risks to technical leads and management.
Collaborate with senior engineers to evaluate potential vendor proposals, software tools, or third-party APIs for system compatibility and performance.
Documentation & Technical Communication 
Draft comprehensive system interface documentation, API specifications, data flow diagrams, and user guides.
Present technical updates, data metrics, and project status briefings to team leads, non-technical stakeholders, and peers.
Prepare clear technical write-ups proposing solutions or corrective actions for data pipeline bottlenecks.
General Team Responsibilities 
Collaborate with fellow developers, systems analysts, and operations personnel to support continuous integration and operational reliability.
Perform code reviews, adhere to standard version control practices, and follow team software development lifecycle (SDLC) standards.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
0-2 years of experience
Core Technical Knowledge: Strong foundational understanding of data structures, algorithms, relational/non-relational databases, and client-server architectures.
Data Interchange & Scripting: Hands-on experience (via coursework, academic projects, or internships) working with structured data formats (XML, JSON, CSV), schema validation (XSD, JSON Schema), and at least one programming/scripting language (e.g., Python, Java, C#, or JavaScript/Node.js).
Database Fundamentals: Proficiency with SQL and querying relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server).
Communication & Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to document code clearly and present technical concepts to peers and project leads.
Tools: Familiarity with modern collaboration suites (Microsoft Office 365, Teams, Slack) and version control platforms (Git/GitHub/GitLab).
Ability to travel up to 15–20% for on-site team planning or stakeholder workshops as required.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Information Systems, or a closely related technical field (graduated within the last 12 months or nearing graduation).
Preferred: 
Exposure to RESTful API design, web services, or middleware/integration platforms.
Experience with ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines or messaging queues.
Prior internship, capstone project, or open-source contribution involving cross-system data transfer or interface design.
Basic understanding of project management methodologies (Agile/Scrum, Jira, Trello).

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
PeopleTec is seeking a Systems Engineer/Analyst to support Missile Defense Agency Systems Engineering Directorate to provide Verification and Validation support for the System Verification Director . This position plays a key role in defining, analyzing, and managing requirements spanning the entire system life cycle - from concept development through testing and deployment.
Duties: 
Develop/maintain code for Ground Test and Flight Test data analysis required by MDA/SEQV. Coordinate with other developers collaborating on code modifications and analysis tools within a code repository of thousands of executable lines of python code housed in a git repository environment.
Write Python, MATLAB, and shell command scripts to verify and validate test system requirements for Missile Defense Elements using Ground Test and Flight Test data.
Execute System Interface Control Document (SICD) requirements checkout using MATLAB requirements analysis code against tactical message log data recorded from flight and ground test data sources.
Develop scripts to import, parse, and extract Missile Defense Data Center (MDDC) ground test and flight test data to be used for MDA/SEQV activities including Threat V&V analysis, Core Truth Model (CTM) analysis, SICD analysis, and System Federation Validation Events (SFVE) / System Post Flight Reconstruction (SPFR) performance parameter analysis.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience in systems engineering supporting missile defense or other complex defense systems.
Must have a strong ability to use Python, MATLAB , and ability to execute operating system shell command scripts 
Strong understanding of MDA system architectures , lifecycle processes, and verification/validation. 
Ability to translate high-level mission objectives into detailed technical requirements.
Excellent analytical, documentation, and communication skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and experience)

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
We are seeking a motivated engineer/analyst to provide Modeling and Simulation (M&S) Verification, Validation, and Accreditation (VV&A) support to the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) System Verification directorate. The selected candidate will serve a lead role for M&S accreditation efforts associated with Aegis BMD, Sensor (e.g., Cobra Dane, UEWR, AN/TPY-2, SBX, LRDR), or other models represented in the MDA Ground Test (GT) events. 
This is a full-time, on-site position at a government customer location. The selected candidate will collaborate with Government customers, internal and external Missile Defense Agency (MDA) stakeholders, program offices, and M&S development prime contractors.
Duties: 
Serve as subject matter expert for information (e.g., M&S versions, V&V plans, M&S versus tactical boundaries) associated with assigned Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) M&S.
Coordinate with model owners to develop executable action plans to ensure timely delivery of V&V evidence supporting accreditation information needs for MDA M&S accreditation assessments of applicable GT data sources.
Conduct technical review of V&V evidence and develop M&S accreditation recommendations for the MDA accreditation authority.
Author sections and/or provide technical input for relevant products such as the MDA M&S accreditation report/briefing, MDA M&S accreditation decision memorandum, and MDA M&S accreditation plan.
Develop Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M) to address high-priority issues affecting M&S accreditation.
Regularly interface with the model owner and V&V agent to address M&S limitations impacting accreditation outcomes. Document and maintain M&S limitation resolution plans in a dedicated online repository for tracking and reporting purposes.
Collaborate with model owners to maintain or refine Performance Parameters, Acceptability Criteria, and Evaluation Methodologies for inclusion in current and future releases of the M&S Accreditation Plan.
Support Operational Capability List (OCL) Working Group (OWG) meetings to brief MDA M&S accreditation status for HWIL models supporting Missile Defense System (MDS) performance assessment of capabilities to be fielded.
Provide regular verbal and written status updates to leadership regarding M&S VV&A areas of responsibility.
Perform other related tasks as assigned by the Director, MDA System Verification or M&S VV&A lead and strategic advisor.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience with modeling and simulation applications.
Knowledge of M&S VV&A principles, methodologies, and accreditation processes.
Experience evaluating technical evidence of complex defense systems, and developing defensible engineering recommendations.
Familiarity with the Missile Defense System architecture and its integrated defense systems.
Ability to independently lead technical assessments, work within a multi-disciplinary team, develop action plans, and communicate status and findings to government leadership.
Strong technical writing, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or related technical discipline.
Desired Skills : 
Top Secret clearance preferred.
Advanced degree in Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Demonstrated experience with the Aegis BMD weapon system and/or Sensor components of the Missile Defense System architecture.
Experience developing or reviewing M&S accreditation plans, V&V reports, accreditation assessments, and technical recommendations.

Excellent communication and presentation skills. 
Ability to lead and work within a multidisciplinary team.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
text:

PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Systems Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Advanced Fires Project Office (AFPO) and Project Director Manager Scalable Hypersonics (PdM SHY) develop, integrate, and transition advanced weapon systems to meet critical Army operational needs. We are seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to serve as a technical leader guiding requirements, architecture, integration, risk management, and test activities across our rapidly expanding hypersonic portfolio.
The Senior Systems Engineer will manage a highly complex technical baseline, lead technical reviews, maintain strict configuration management, and advise government leadership on engineering risks and opportunities. Crucially, this role will deconflict overlapping technical efforts and resource demands across hypersonic programs (including MROM, ASHS, AHSS, Mach XL, Sirena, and PrsM Inc 4) to ensure responsible stewardship of USG resources.
Duties: 
Lead the development, validation, and maintenance of system requirements, system architecture, and rigorous traceability across the hypersonic portfolio. 
Serve as the primary Risk Manager, establishing risk mitigation strategies and advising program leadership on system engineering risks, opportunities, and trade-offs.

Plan and orchestrate key technical milestones, Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs), and formal technical reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR) to objectively assess system maturity and vendor readiness. 
Deconflict overlapping technical efforts, resource demands, and schedules among the MROM, ASHS, AHSS, Mach XL, Sirena, and PrsM Inc 4 programs. 
Guide system integration efforts and oversee technical performance analyses for prototype and fielded systems.

Proficiency in systems engineering methodologies, digital engineering tools, and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) practices. 
Proven capability to brief senior Army and DoD leadership effectively. 
Strong organizational and leadership skills to coordinate across multi-disciplinary engineering teams and multi-program efforts.

Experience with hypersonic technologies, high-speed flight systems, directed energy, or advanced precision fires programs. 
Active TS/SCI clearance. 
Deep familiarity with Army acquisition pathways, rapid prototyping, Middle Tier of Acquisition (MTA), and rapid fielding initiatives. 
Experience deconflicting resource constraints and technical baselines across joint/parallel vendor efforts.

Sound oral communication and technical writing skills and the ability to clearly communicate technical approaches and findings to the team and the government customer

Bachelor’s degree in science or engineering or scientific field of study from an accredited college or university and 5 - 8+ years of progressively complex experience in modeling and simulation, software, aerospace systems, and/or flight testing

A relevant PhD degree in engineering or science from an accredited college or university may be substituted for three years of relevant work experience.

text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Contract Operations and Systems Specialist  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Contract Operations and Systems Specialist supports our Huntsville, AL location by providing contracting, procurement-policy, compliance, and operational support to a government contracting office. The position requires the skill set of an experienced Contract Specialist with an emphasis on preparing contractual and supporting acquisition documentation, maintaining file integrity and audit readiness, and supporting contracting-office administration. Working onsite as an integral member of the contracting team, the specialist researches and applies acquisition regulations and policy, drafts and reviews documentation for government approval, maintains electronic contract and agreement files, supports tasker and acquisition-system administration, and keeps the office's SharePoint content, trackers, permissions, and existing workflows current.
DUTIES: 
Draft, revise, and format contractual and supporting acquisition documentation for government review and approval, and research and apply applicable acquisition regulations, policy, and local procedures.
Review contractual and acquisition documentation for completeness, consistency, required approvals, and compliance with applicable policy and office procedures; identify deficiencies and track corrective actions to closure.

Maintain workload and suspense trackers; log, route, and track ETMS2 and other office taskers; prepare status information; and alert leadership to late or at-risk actions.

Strong working knowledge of federal and Department of Defense contracting principles, terminology, documentation, and electronic contract-file requirements.
Exceptional written communication and document-development skills, with the ability to produce clear, accurate, and compliant contractual and administrative products.
Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, and judgment when handling sensitive acquisition information and competing suspense dates.
Experience working independently in a deadline-driven contracting office and coordinating actions across multiple organizations and levels of leadership.
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, Adobe Acrobat, and SharePoint content maintenance.
Ability to maintain existing SharePoint libraries, lists, metadata, permissions requests, trackers, and workflows; advanced SharePoint development is not required.

title: Senior Datalinks Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Datalinks Engineer  to support our Huntsvile, AL location.
We are seeking a highly capable Senior Datalinks Engineer to support the PM UAS Technical Management Division (TMD) and serve as the primary Division-level technical expert for UAS datalinks. This individual will work in direct support of the Chief Engineer, the PM UAS Product Offices, the Component Technology Branch, and special projects aligned with the PM UAS mission.
The Senior Datalinks Engineer will serve as the primary datalinks subject matter expert for PM UAS at the Division level, supporting the Chief Engineer and providing technical leadership across the PM UAS enterprise. The individual will provide technical oversight and subject matter expertise for UAS datalink system development, integration, qualification, fielding, sustainment, modernization, and issue resolution. Relevant technologies include:
Modems and radio frequency (RF) equipment
Antennas and radomes
RF interfaces and architectures
Communication protocols
Datalink standards
Software and firmware
Waveforms
Frequency management
EMI/EMV design and qualification
Electronic warfare (EW) hardening and resiliency
RF modeling and analysis
Encryption, including AES-256 and Type 1 encryption concepts
Communications Security (COMSEC)
Transmission Security (TRANSEC)
The ideal candidate will combine significant RF/datalink technical expertise with strong systems engineering judgment, strategic thinking, acquisition awareness, communication skills, and the ability to lead through complex technical and organizational challenges.
Duties: 
Develop and coordinate a comprehensive UAS datalink strategy consistent with PM UAS objectives, missions, architectures, and future capabilities.
Serve as the principal datalink technical advisor to the Chief Engineer, TMD leadership, Product Offices, and other PM UAS stakeholders.
Provide technical oversight for datalink system development, integration, qualification, production, fielding, modernization, and sustainment.
Evaluate systems, subsystems, and components involving RF equipment, antennas, modems, radomes, communications protocols, interfaces, software, waveforms, and associated technologies.
Assess relevant threat environments and evaluate potential impacts to UAS RF and communications systems.
Evaluate datalink resiliency, interoperability, spectrum, encryption, COMSEC, TRANSEC, EMI/EMV, and EW considerations.
Support technical assessments of current and emerging datalink capabilities, technologies, standards, and architectures.

text:

PeopleTec is currently seeking a Special Programs Integration Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Special Programs Integration Engineer serves as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Offensive Fires Command and Control (C2) Integration within the Product Manager Scalable Hypersonics (PdM SHY). Addressing a critical capability gap, this role provides technical leadership, C2 integration oversight, and systems engineering support across three active and expanding hypersonic missile programs. 
The primary focus is driving the near-term priority, Medium Range Offensive Munition (MROM) , by overseeing the complex integration of the Blackbeard hypersonic missile onto the HIMARS launch platform and subsequently onto the CAML launcher . The SME will spearhead intense coordination and technical collaboration across key external stakeholders, including PM STORM, the Software, Simulation, Systems Engineering and Integration (S3I) software development team, and PdM SHY leadership
DUTIES: 
Offensive Fires C2 Integration: Serve as the primary C2 Integration SME overseeing system architecture, software alignment, and tactical control capabilities across PdM SHY's hypersonic missile programs. 
MROM & Blackbeard Program Execution: Direct the technical integration of the Blackbeard hypersonic missile onto the HIMARS launch platform and manage follow-on integration efforts onto the CAML launcher in support of the MROM priority. 
Cross-Stakeholder Synchronization: Lead intense coordination and technical collaboration with PM STORM, the S3I software development team, PdM SHY, government matrix engineering teams, and industry partners. 
System-of-Systems Interface Alignment: Develop, refine, and validate interface requirements, Interface Control Documents (ICDs), and Concepts of Operation (CONOPS) for C2, missile, and launcher integration. 
Engineering Analysis & Technical Trade Studies: Conduct feasibility assessments, software/hardware trade studies, and integration evaluations to ensure seamless interoperability between launch platforms, C2 architectures, and strike weapon systems. 
Special Programs & Technical Oversight: Provide engineering support for sensitive, high-priority hypersonic and offensive fires initiatives within special access environments. 
Executive Decision Products: Prepare technical briefings, integration roadmaps, software interface specifications, and risk assessments for PdM SHY, PM STORM, and senior DoD leadership.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
7–10+ years of progressive engineering, technical project management, or system integration experience within DoD, U.S. Army, or Joint weapon system program offices. 
Offensive Fires & C2 Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in Command & Control (C2) systems integration, launch platform interfaces, or tactical fires software. 
System Engineering & Architecture: Strong background in systems engineering, requirements definition, software/hardware interface control (ICDs), and complex system-of-systems integration. 
Multi-Agency Stakeholder Coordination: Proven ability to drive consensus and lead complex integration efforts across external PMs, software centers (e.g., S3I), and cross-functional government teams. 
Communication: Exceptional oral and written communication skills with experience presenting technical decision products to senior Army and DoD leadership. 
Tools: Proficiency with standard Microsoft Office products (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Project). 
Must possess a valid driver's license
Travel: 10%
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Top Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active DoD Top Secret / SCI with Special Access Required (TS/SCI/SAR) upon hire , and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Aerospace, Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, Software) or a closely related technical field. 
Master’s degree preferred.

Direct experience with PdM Scalable Hypersonics (SHY) programs (MROM, Blackbeard, CAML, Sirena, or ASHS).

title: Project Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Project Engineer to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Project Engineer provides dedicated technical expertise, engineering integration, and project management support for Product Manager Scalable Hypersonics (PdM SHY). The position supports active and expanding missile programs, including Medium Range Offensive Munition (MROM), Advanced Short-Range Hypersonic (ASHS), and the transition of the Sirena program. This role ensures engineering rigor, interface alignment, and technical coherence for hypersonic systems, weapon launchers, and fire control integration. The Project Engineer translates complex technical data into actionable decisions for PdM SHY leadership and supports offsite coordination, testing, and fielding activities.
Duties:  
Technical & Weapons Integration: Support engineering integration for PdM SHY programs (MROM, ASHS, Sirena), with an emphasis on weapons integration, weapon launchers, fire control software, and aerodynamics. 
Requirements & Interface Management: Develop, refine, and validate system requirements; manage technical interfaces; ensure interoperability across missile subsystems, launchers, and supporting fire control architecture. 
Engineering & Trade Studies: Conduct engineering assessments, trade studies, and technical evaluations regarding aerodynamics, launcher mechanics, and integration risks to support design decisions and program execution. 
Test & Evaluation Support: Assist in test engineering and the planning and execution of developmental and operational testing for SHY programs; review test data and track technical issues through resolution. 
Risk & Safety Management: Identify technical risks, system integration challenges, and safety/schedule risks across active SHY missile efforts; recommend engineering mitigations and solutions. 
Technical Documentation & Reporting: Prepare engineering reports, interface documents, technical briefings, and review materials required for PdM SHY leadership and stakeholder engagements. 
Stakeholder & Offsite Coordination: Coordinate offsite SHY activities and liaise with matrixed Government engineering teams, prime contractors, and external program partners. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
7–10+ years of engineering experience in DoD, Army, or Joint missile/fires programs. 
Direct experience in weapons integration, weapon launcher systems, fire control software, aerodynamics, test engineering, and systems integration . 
Strong background in systems engineering, integration, or technical project management supporting complex missile programs. 
Experience developing and managing system requirements, interfaces, and technical documentation. 
Demonstrated ability to coordinate across diverse technical teams, offsite facilities, and external stakeholders. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to prepare senior-level technical briefings. 
Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook). 
Must have a current driver’s license. 
Travel: 10–20% (including offsite SHY facility/test coordination). 
Must be a U.S. Citizen. 
Active DoD Top Secret / SCI / Special Access Required (TS/SCI/SAR) upon hire
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, Aerospace, or related field).
Master’s degree preferred.
Desired Skills : 
Specific experience supporting PdM Scalable Hypersonics (SHY) or hypersonic/offensive fires program offices (MROM, ASHS, Sirena). 
Background in launcher integration and fire control software architecture. 
Experience working within PEO Missiles & Space, RCCTO, or AFPO organizations. 
Self-starter capable of managing multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment

title: Network Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Network Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The candidate will serve as a Network Engineer within a Project Management Office (PMO) within PAE Fires and will be responsible for providing technical support to the program's Chief Engineer and the Product Manager. The candidate will provide network engineering expertise across the life cycle of tactical network capabilities integrated into Army Fires’ air defense weapon systems, spanning design, development, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment of network transport, data links, and secure information exchange. Work will emphasize LAN and WAN performance, secure information sharing across classification domains, cryptographic and communications security (COMSEC) integration, and technology refresh of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) network components driven by obsolescence and cybersecurity compliance. The candidate will prepare and present network findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Will work within and/or lead a multidisciplinary team to achieve program goals. Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager. 
The candidate will interface with internal PMs across PAE Fires and external organizations to include HQDA, ASA(ALT), AvMC, ATEC, AMCOM, multiple Cross-Functional Teams, and others for coordination and synchronization of network technical and programmatic objectives. 
Duties: 
Provide network engineering support across the life cycle (design, development, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment) of tactical network capabilities integrated into PAE Fires air defense weapon systems. 
Plan and execute network and data link tests to assess and advance the capabilities of current and future operations across product office weapon systems. 
Analyze requirements documents, interpret technical and programmatic needs, and manage supplier network solutions for weapon system tactical networks and battlefield data dissemination across multiple networks. 
Provide technical expertise on networks and their components that integrate sensors, effectors, and fire control systems into a system of systems, including the configuration, installation, troubleshooting, and operation of the network topology. 
Support secure information exchange between networks operating at different classification levels, including cross-domain solution integration, security policy enforcement, and auditability. 
Oversee information classification and encryption or COMSEC requirements in support of Government solutions. 
Support technology refresh and obsolescence management of COTS network components to sustain compliant, supportable capability and maintain a viable authority to operate. 
Troubleshoot and sustain LAN and WAN operations, including simulated and test environments, and analyze real-world communication and performance issues. 
Develop and review technical documentation supporting installation, configuration, and troubleshooting of network equipment. 
Prepare and present network findings, reports, and improvement plans to management and stakeholders. 
Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5+ years of relevant network engineering experience. Additional education may be substituted for years of experience. 
Hands-on experience with LAN and WAN design, switching and routing, and network troubleshooting, particularly within defense environments. 
Experience with tactical network solutions, including their design, integration, and sustainment in support of weapon system operations. 
Working knowledge of network security, information assurance, and IAVA and RMF compliance. 
Familiarity with cryptographic and COMSEC devices and secure data transfer across classification domains. 
Strong knowledge of industry standards and defense requirements. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills. 
Ability to lead and work within a multidisciplinary team. 
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance (with TS/SCI eligibility). 
Education Requirements: 
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline (for example, computer science or information technology); advanced degree preferred. 
Desired Experience: 
Previous experience working in or supporting a U.S. Government Program Office (preferred). 
Industry networking certifications such as CCNA or CCNP. 
Experience with cross-domain solutions, Army tactical networks and their components. 
Familiarity with Army acquisition processes and PAE Fires air defense programs.

title: Business and Financial Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support the Army’s Portfolio Acquisition Executive Fires Office (PAE Fires). This role involves leading budget formulation, execution, and reporting activities to ensure the effective allocation and utilization of resources in support of mission objectives. The Budget Analyst will collaborate with program managers, contracting officers, and other stakeholders to ensure compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) financial regulations and policies. This is a fast-paced role requiring strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
Duties: 
Develop, prepare, and manage program budgets, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submissions, spend plans, and obligation/expenditure forecasts.
Coordinate and execute funding actions, including drafting and submitting Purchase Requisitions (PRs), Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests (MIPRs), and Direct Charge (DC) transactions.
Monitor and track the execution of funds to ensure alignment with program goals and timelines.
Conduct detailed financial analyses to identify trends, variances, and risks.
Prepare and present financial reports, briefings, and recommendations to leadership and stakeholders.
Maintain historical financial records and update funding history tracking when funds are received.
Monitor contract status, including ceiling limits, periods of performance, and funding requirements.
Support Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs) by analyzing monthly contractor reports, facilitating communication, and supporting  documentation for contract actions (e.g. Technical Directives (TDs) and Requests for Services Contract Approval (RSCAs).
Participate in Contract Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Program Management Reviews (PMRs), and financial/metrics meetings.
Ensure compliance with DoD financial management regulations, policies, and procedures.
Facilitate fiscal year-end close to ensure 100% obligation of expiring funds.
Support audits and reviews by providing accurate and timely financial data.
Coordinate with program managers and technical leads to align financial plans with program objectives.
Facilitate financial communication and coordination between the Project Office, higher headquarters, and external customers.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in budget analysis, financial management, or related roles, preferably within the DoD or federal government.

Publishing integration status reports, test readiness documentation, and briefing materials summarizing analysis results.

title: STUDENT TRAINEE (OPERATIONS RESEARCH)
location: Redstone Arsenal, Alabama; Los Angeles County, California; Colorado Springs, Colorado; Patrick AFB, Florida; Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio; Arlington, Virginia; Fort Belvoir, Virginia
text:
The DoW College Acquisition Internship Program (DCAIP) is a paid, 10- to 12- week summer internship that provides students with real-world exposure to Department of War acquisition workforce career opportunities. The program targets full-time second and third year students currently enrolled in an undergraduate program at an accredited college or university.
Qualifications: Requirements: Enrolled or formally accepted for enrollment as a full-time student into an accredited college or university in a qualifying degree-seeking program, or enrolled or formally accepted for enrollment in a qualifying certificate program. Be enrolled full-time as a sophomore or junior in an undergraduate program at an accredited university and have completed a minimum of 24 credit hours toward a specific degree program. Students must have a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent) at time of application and must maintain at least a 3.0 GPA throughout the entire Student Trainee Internship appointment to remain in the Program. Please note that if you are graduating from your current academic program prior to May 31, 2027 you will not be eligible for this student appointment unless you are accepted for enrollment at a qualifying educational institution seeking an ADDITIONAL qualifying degree, diploma, certificate, etc. You MUST submit proof of acceptance along with your current transcripts for consideration.
Education: Due to the education requirement of this position, an official or unofficial transcript must be submitted at the time of application. If transcripts are not received, you will be rated as ineligible. Accreditation: Only degrees from an accredited college or university recognized by the Department of Education are acceptable to meet positive education requirements or to substitute for experience. For additional information, please go to the Office of Personnel Management website at http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/Standards/group-stds/gs-prof.asp and U.S. Department of Education website at http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/Search.aspx Special Instructions for Foreign Education: Education completed in foreign colleges or universities must be evaluated in terms of equivalency to that acquired in U.S. colleges and universities. Applicants educated in whole or in part in foreign countries must submit sufficient evidence, including transcripts, to an accredited private organization for an equivalency evaluation of course work and degree. A listing of these accredited organizations can be found on the Department of Education's website. You must provide a copy of the letter containing the results of the equivalency evaluation with a course by course listing along with your application. If you fail to provide the required documentation, by the closing date of this announcement, you will not receive consideration. For further information, visit: https://www.ed.gov/about/initiatives/international-affairs/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications
Requirements: 
As a STUDENT TRAINEE (OPERATIONS RESEARCH), duties will depend on your major and the Program Office. The selected candidate(s) may be placed within one of the Program Offices based on the office's function and the student's major, skill sets and interest. Interns receive hands-on, practical experience in analysis, research, report writing, oral briefings, policy development, program analysis, and computer applications. Student interns gain experience in career fields available within the Acquisition workforce such as: Engineering, Contracting, Logistics, Business - Financial Management, Business - Cost Estimating, Information Technology, Test & Evaluation, Industrial Contract Property Management, Purchasing, Science and Technology, Production, Quality and Manufacturing, Facilities Engineering, and Program Management.
Security clearance: Secret.

company: George C. Marshall Space Flight Center (federal)
title: Manager, Space Launch Systems Program
text:
The Manager, Space Launch System Program (SLSP) Office, is responsible for safety and mission success of the Space Launch System (SLS) with authority for all activities associated with the programmatic, fiscal, and technical planning, procurement, design, development, testing, evaluation, production, and operation of the integrated SLS, including support equipment and facilities.
Qualifications: As a basic requirement for entry into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment, you must clearly articulate and describe within your 2-page resume that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) and Mandatory Technical Qualifications MTQ(s) related to this position. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and MTQ(s), you may be disqualified. Any additional pages over the 2-page limit will not be reviewed. Your resume should include evidence of progressively responsible supervisory, managerial, or professional experience which involved management of a program or organization of significant scope and complexity, normally obtained over several years by serving in positions at the GS-15 level or equivalent. If you are (1) currently serving under a career SES appointment, (2) eligible for reinstatement into the SES (this means you were previously employed as a Career SES employee and you successfully completed a one-year probationary period), OR (3) have successfully completed a SES Candidate Development Program (CDP) and certified by OPM, you do not need to address the ECQs in your resume. However, your resume must clearly state that you are a current career SES, eligible for SES reinstatement, or SES CDP certified and year of certification. Please DO NOT submit separate documents addressing the ECQs or MTQ(s). Only your 2-page resume will be accepted and considered. Any additional documents submitted will not be accepted. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs) For more information on the ECQs, please visit OPM's ECQ webpage. ECQ 1 - Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government, Commitment to the Rule of Law, and Civic-Mindedness ECQ 2 - Driving Efficiency: This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility, Managing Resources, Leveraging Technology ECQ 3 - Merit and Competence: This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Competencies: Technical Skill, Problem Solving, Agility and Resilience ECQ 4 - Leading People: This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. Competencies: Accountability, Developing Others, Executive Judgment ECQ 5 - Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Competencies: Operational Mindset, Innovation, Strategic Thinking MANDATORY TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (MTQ): Your resume must include accomplishments that address the MTQ(s). MTQ: Demonstrated experience leading the design, integration, testing, certification, and operational deployment of space vehicles, or large-scale complex systems, as well as managing large-scale spaceflight projects/programs-including budget development/management, acquisition planning, resource allocation, cost control, risk management, and alignment of program requirements with agency goals and schedules. Competencies: Program/Project Management, Risk Management and Financial Management Your application package must be in your own words. Experience statements copied from a position description, vacancy announcement, or other reference material constitutes plagiarism and may result in disqualification and losing consideration for the job. Please visit https://www.nasa.gov/careers/how-to-apply/#Artificial-Intelligence to review NASA's guidance on the use of artificial intelligent (AI) or AI-assisted tools during the application process.
Education: This position has a positive education requirement. To be eligible, you must clearly state in your resume the following: degree, major and/or minor, and college/university. A college or university degree generally must be from an accredited (or pre-accredited) college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. For a list of schools which meet these criteria, please refer to Department of Education Accreditation page. A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major study in engineering, physical science, mathematics, life sciences, computer science, or other field of science is required. An official transcript will be required if you are selected. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show that the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs. These education credentials must be deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, click here.
Requirements: 
The Manager, Space Launch Systems Program: Integrates with the Artemis Program and serves as a senior member of its executive team. Formulates program budget requirements and requests, phasing plans, schedules, and workforce requirements necessary for the successful execution of the design, development, and fielding of an integrated SLS. Manages NASA and contractor activities throughout the development life cycle leading to a fully integrated and functional flight vehicle. Formulates and implements program policy; defines and controls system architecture; establishes and controls program-level requirements, system configuration, and schedule; plans and directs the program's development, test, production, and operations activities; manages the integration of all program elements into a single operational system to include all necessary and applicable launch system certifications; and ensures effective cost control of the total program. Defines and recommends SLSP resource requirements, including construction of facilities requirements. Ensures integration between the SLSP and its payloads, including the Orion Spacecraft and ground processing, launch, and mission operations. Administers the SLS manifest and mission assignments. Chairs the SLSP Control Board to manage program requirements, appropriate requirements waivers and anomalies, applicable flight definition requirements document changes, and authorization for program adjustment. Serves as programmatic and technical advisor to the Artemis Program Manager, other Agency officials, and senior leadership across a wide spectrum of industrial and governmental institutions and international partners. Represents the SLSP on Agency actions, special studies, governmental audits, independent assessments and reviews, and meeting other performance reporting requirements. Also serves as chair or member of various panels, participates in conferences and working groups, and serves on technical committees as assigned.

text:
THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a SURFACE MAINTENANCE REPAIRER (T32), Position Description Number D1193000 and is part of the AL UTES 3, National Guard. ORGANIZATION: AL UTES 3, HUNTSVILLE, AL SELECTING OFFICIAL: CW4 F. PEPPER
Qualifications: MILITARY REQUIREMENTS: This is an excepted service position that requires membership in a compatible military grade in the Alabama Army National Guard. Applicants who are not currently a member of the Alabama Army National Guard must be eligible for immediate membership. If you are not sure you are eligible for military membership, please contact an Alabama Army National Guard recruiter at 800-464-8273 prior to applying for this position. MINIMUM MILITARY RANK: PVT MAXIMUM MILITARY RANK: SFC EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: Each applicant must fully substantiate (in his/her own words) that he/she meets the requirements of the Specialized Experience listed below: Otherwise, the applicant will be considered unqualified for this position. DO NOT COPY THE VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT OR THE POSITION DESCRIPTION. DOING SO MAY RESULT IN DISQUALIFICATION FOR THE POSITION. GENERAL EXPERIENCE: Experience or training which demonstrates knowledge of equipment to be able to do routine jobs, simple preventative maintenance tasks, and can use common tools and equipment in the line of work. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Experience or training using common hand and power tools and a small variety of test and measurement devices to make mechanical repairs. Experience removing, adjusting, replacing, cleaning, and installing a variety of parts, components, and accessories. Experience which demonstrates a basic understanding of mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic theory applying to vehicles; and skill to replace, fit, install, and make adjustments. Experience demonstrating an understanding of the makeup and operation of the various individual systems maintained and their interrelationships. Experience reading and interpreting parts lists, manufactures' repair manuals, diagrams, and electrical schematics. SKILL AND KNOWLEDGE: -- Basic knowledge and understanding of the mechanical makeup, operation, and working relationships of individual systems, and their interrelationships for a variety of combat, tactical, commercial, automotive, special purpose vehicles and equipment. -- Working knowledge of various techniques for removing, adjusting, replacing, cleaning, and installing parts and components of combat, tactical, commercial, automotive, special purpose vehicles and equipment. -- Basic understanding of electrical, electronic, hydraulic, pneumatic, and other non-mechanical system theories; and skill to replace, fit, install, and adjust systems. -- Skill to use basic test equipment and ability to analyze test results to determine fault for repair or replacement of improperly functioning parts or components. Ability to use basic tools common to the occupation. -- Ability to determine when parts should be cleaned, reinstalled, or replaced with standard parts. -- Ability to read and interpret parts list, manufacturer's repair manuals, technical manuals, diagrams, engineering drawings, and schematics.
Education: SUBSTITUTION OF EDUCATION IS NOT CONSIDERED FOR WAGE GRADE POSITIONS.
Requirements: 
(1) Performs limited diagnosis, routine repairs and maintenance on heavy-duty mobile equipment, combat, tactical and automotive vehicles. Assists higher graded mechanics in the repair and/or overhaul of major systems to include internal combustion engines, turbine engines, automatic and non-automatic transmissions, heavy duty drive line systems, and hydraulic utility systems and controls. Makes routine repairs that can be accomplished by removing, adjusting, or replacing defective or worn parts and components. Performs work in accordance with technical manuals, lubrication orders, maintenance bulletins, regulations or management policies. (2) Performs limited diagnoses to determine the cause of mechanical failures by means of visual and auditory checks and/or uses basic test equipment such as compression testers, voltmeters, ohmmeters and pressure gauges. Determines when parts should be cleaned, adjusted or replaced with standard parts to complete work orders. (3) Removes, replaces, adjusts, cleans and installs parts and components such as wheel seals, switches, sensors, fuel pumps, water pumps, power steering pumps, brakes, filters, radiators, bearings, springs, shock absorbers, wheel cylinders, starter motors, mufflers, battery cables, and other items of similar complexity. (4) Independently performs routine repairs and maintenance functions in remote locations that can be accomplished by removing, cleaning, reinstalling, or replacing defective parts of components and systems using standard parts. Receives guidance and instruction from a higher graded mechanic or supervisor to perform non-routine and more complex repairs on portions of major assemblies and/or systems. May provide field maintenance at unit locations as part of a "contact team". Recovers and evacuates inoperable vehicles from the unit location of breakdown. (5) Conducts limited readiness and repair inspections on vehicles and associated equipment supported by the activity. Performs Preventive Maintenance Checks and Services (PMCS) and ensures vehicles and equipment are properly serviced, including brake adjustments, replacing hydraulic fluids, greasing, cleaning, etc. Performs other preventive maintenance operations as required to ensure that equipment is functioning properly. (6) May perform routine maintenance and limited repairs on basic communication equipment such as radios, field telephones, amplifiers, switchboards, recorders, intercoms by removing and replacing components and elements. Performs minor body and fender, or other metal repairs, using peening hammers, dollies and limited welding. Performs limited repairs and routine maintenance on small arms and accessory equipment by replacing worn or damaged parts. Makes minor repairs to canvas and leather items using bonding/sealing compounds and hand tools such as awls, canvas needles etc. (7) In conjunction with or in the absence of the Tools and Parts Attendant, may maintain supply documentation, and the receipt, store, issue, and inventory of tools and parts used in the trades operation. (8) Performs other duties as assigned.

About the Position: This position serves as an Information Technology Specialist (INFOSEC) for the US Army Corps of Engineers, acting as a subject matter expert on cyber security intelligence to enhance the organization's security posture. The role involves analyzing network threats, conducting counterintelligence and criminal investigations into computer intrusions, and implementing new security measures to protect IT systems.
Qualifications: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Specialized Experience GS-13: One year of specialized experience which includes:1) Serving as a subject matter expert on cyber security intelligence, performing activities to gather and preserve evidence on criminal or foreign intelligence entities to mitigate real-time threats and support the prosecution of computer crimes. 2) Analyzing computer-generated threats, log files, and collected evidence to identify network intruders, and fusing computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations and operations. 3) Enhancing cyber security capabilities by evaluating security architectures, integrating security policy into IT systems, and managing the procurement and implementation of new security tools and systems in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) and Army regulations. 4) Developing and presenting technical briefings, presentations, and reports on IT security status, weaknesses, and recommended courses of action to organizational leadership and external stakeholders. All experience areas shall additionally demonstrate each of the following competencies: 1) Attention to Detail, 2) Customer Service, 3) Oral Communication, and 4) Problem Solving. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate. Fuse computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations to support legal and operational actions.
Monitor external data sources to maintain an up-to-date understanding of cyber threat conditions and their potential impact on the enterprise.
Analyze computer-generated threats, log files, and collected evidence to identify the perpetrators of network intrusions.
Gather evidence on criminal or foreign intelligence entities to mitigate real-time threats and support the prosecution of computer crimes.

To be acceptable, the program must:(1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. You will evaluate contractor proposals and engineering change proposals, providing technical recommendations to the program office on labor hours, materials, and production impacts.
You will oversee hardware configuration audits, initial production inspections, and acceptance reviews to verify prototype and production hardware meets engineering specifications before government acceptance.
